1	# walker-TANK
2	
3	A tank-battle game in Godot: you drive **YunqiZ** through a ruined brick battlefield and destroy three enemy tanks.
4	
5	- **Starting point:** my own Assignment 2 game and Assignment 3 3D asset room in this repository (A5 baseline commit `c4a1f84`). See [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).
6	- **Engine:** Godot 4.7.2 stable. **Renderer:** Forward+ (engine default; `project.godot` sets no renderer). 2D: 1280×720, stretch `canvas_items`, no `hdr_2d`.
7	- **Film (Assignment 5):** TBD.
8	
9	## Assignment 5 — hit flash shader and brick surface materials
10	
11	### What Assignment 5 added
12	
13	- **Hit flash on YunqiZ (2D):** `shaders/hit_flash.gdshader` (`canvas_item`, hand-written by me) mixes the sprite colour toward red: `mix(COLOR.rgb, flash_color.rgb, hit_amount * flash_strength)`. `scripts/hit_flash_driver.gd`, attached by one line in `scripts/main.gd`, puts one shared ShaderMaterial on YunqiZ's hull and turret.
14	  - On `damaged` it sets `hit_amount` to 1.0, then fades it to 0.0 over 0.5 s of game time.
15	  - A new hit restarts the fade. Pause holds it. Death and respawn clear it.
16	  - Enemies have no material. The existing white `_flash()` is unchanged.
17	- **Brick materials (3D):** `shaders/brick_surface.gdshader` (`spatial`, hand-written by me). It projects the Poly Haven red_bricks_04 colour and roughness maps from object-space position, because `cover_wall.glb` has no UVs. Uniforms: `albedo_tint`, `brightness`, `roughness_scale`, `uv_scale`.
18	  - Two materials share it: `materials/cover_wall_intact.tres` on `CoverWall` (through the importer's Use External on `M_Brick`) and `materials/cover_wall_damaged.tres` on a new `CoverWall2` (surface override).
19	- **Hint experiment:** `scenes/hint_experiment.tscn` with `shaders/hint_experiment.gdshader`. It shows the same 3×1 grey PNG (64/128/192, `tools/make_hint_png.gd`) through a sampler with `source_color` (Quad A) and one without (Quad B).
20	- **Generated shader for comparison:** `shaders/standard_generated.gdshader` (Godot's *Convert to ShaderMaterial* in `scenes/scratch_standard.tscn`; not used by the game).
21	- **Tests:** `tests/test_hit_flash.gd`, `tests/test_materials.gd`, `tests/check_tools_parse.gd`. **Capture tools:** `tools/capture_hit_flash.gd`, `tools/capture_hint.gd`, `tools/capture_materials.gd`.
22	- **Documents:** [CHANGE-BRIEF](CHANGE-BRIEF.md) (with Revisions) · [TEST-REPORT](TEST-REPORT.md) · [MATERIALS](MATERIALS.md) · [LANGUAGE-NOTES](LANGUAGE-NOTES.md) · [FRICTIONAL](FRICTIONAL.md) · [SOURCES](SOURCES.md) · [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). Evidence: `logs/`, `docs/a5/`.
23	
24	### Run (Windows, Git Bash, from the repo root)
25	
26	```bash
27	GODOT="/d/CSYE7270/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe"   # as in scripts/run-test.sh line 5
28	
29	# Import once after cloning
30	"$GODOT" --headless --path . --import
31	
32	# The game (main scene, scenes/main.tscn); or open the project in the editor and press F5
33	"$GODOT" --path .
34	
35	# The 3D asset room with the two brick walls; or open the scene in the editor and press F6
36	"$GODOT" --path . res://scenes/asset_room_3d.tscn
37	
38	# The hint experiment
39	"$GODOT" --path . res://scenes/hint_experiment.tscn
40	```
41	
42	**Tests**, always through the wrapper, one per call. The wrapper runs headless with `--fixed-fps`, a 120 s timeout, and a log in `logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log`. It exits 1 on any FAIL or on `SHADER ERROR` / `SCRIPT ERROR`.
43	
44	```bash
45	bash scripts/run-test.sh test_hit_flash.gd 30
46	bash scripts/run-test.sh test_hit_flash.gd 60
47	bash scripts/run-test.sh test_hit_flash.gd 144
48	bash scripts/run-test.sh test_materials.gd 60
49	bash scripts/run-test.sh check_tools_parse.gd 60
50	bash scripts/run-test.sh check_a3_assets.gd 60
51	bash scripts/run-test.sh test_sound_triggers.gd 60
52	```
53	
54	Results at `3d48047`: 50/50 at each rate, 76/76, 9/9, 18/18, 8/8, all exit 0 ([TEST-REPORT](TEST-REPORT.md)).
55	
56	**Capture tools.** These need a real window, because headless draws nothing. Output goes to `docs/a5/captures/`.
57	
58	```bash
59	"$GODOT" --path . --resolution 1280x720 --script res://tools/capture_hit_flash.gd
60	"$GODOT" --path . --resolution 1280x720 --script res://tools/capture_hint.gd
61	"$GODOT" --path . --resolution 1280x720 --script res://tools/capture_materials.gd
62	# optional: prefix every file, e.g. after a temporary shader edit
63	"$GODOT" --path . --resolution 1280x720 --script res://tools/capture_materials.gd -- --tag=shader_edit
64	```
65	
66	The game and the two scenes can also be opened in the editor. The command-line scene runs above follow Godot's standard CLI and were not themselves recorded in my notes.
67	
68	### Controls
69	
70	Unchanged from Assignment 2 (table below): WASD / arrows move, mouse aims, left mouse / Space fires, Esc / P pauses, M / N mute music / SFX, R restarts after victory.
71	
72	### Known limitations (A5, from my notes)
73	
74	- The existing white `_flash()` still runs (the test sees modulate 2.2), but in play it is visually masked by the red at the moment of the hit.
75	- The pause rule (fade holds while paused) has only the headless check. I could not press Esc within 0.5 s.
76	- `reset_full()` on a living tank mid-fade would not clear the fade. The game only calls it after death.
77	- My named pixel P1 is covered by the turret. The brief's hull prediction does not apply there, and a recomputed turret value is in the brief's Revisions. P2 matched exactly.
78	- No game material uses a normal map. `red_bricks_04_nor_gl_1k.png` is only in the Step 4 scratch material, so the normal-map check is not applicable.
79	- The interface-sweep looks (wash-out, gloss, brick size) are recorded mostly as numbers. Several are still to confirm by eye.
80	- The helper bash/python scripts I ran were written by Claude chat and are not in the repo.
81	
82	---
83	
84	## Assignment 3
85	
86	Assignment 3 adds a 3D asset room to this repository; the 2D game from Assignment 2 (below) is unchanged.
87	
88	- **3D asset room:** `scenes/asset_room_3d.tscn` puts the three assets next to a grey 6.0 × 1.6 × 3.4 m box that stands in for the YunqiZ hull, under one light.
89	- **Three assets**, built from Blender cubes, 36 triangles each, exported to `assets/models/`:
90	  - `cover_wall` — broken brick cover wall, 4.0 × 1.0 × 1.8 m (includes one hand edit of my own)
91	  - `ammo_crate` — olive crate with an off-white stripe, 1.24 × 0.84 × 0.71 m
92	  - `tank_hedgehog` — three crossed steel beams, 1.794 × 1.794 × 1.400 m
93	- **Build and export scripts:** `tools/blender/build_cover_wall.py`, `build_ammo_crate.py`, `build_tank_hedgehog.py` rebuild each asset from nothing and check it; `tools/blender/export_glb.py` exports a `.blend` to `.glb`.
94	- **Headless check:** `tests/check_a3_assets.gd` measures each `.glb` in Godot (size, lowest Y, root scale, height axis): 18 / 18 PASS.
95	- **Final film:** [Watch on Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tCX0BUF_Jx4Uj2bW2vaNanxA3WYCKaQn/view?usp=drive_link) — `claude-liam-walker-tank-a3-assets.mp4` (3840×2160 landscape, 3:39), SHA-256 `b91f985d83d7ffed36f941aef078ee3efa676d958c6f58b1ad84931d95c98d8c`. It shows game-source revision `9baa12c`. Its beat sheet, script and evidence are in `youtube/claude-liam-walker-tank-a3-assets/`; the MP4 itself is not in Git.
96	
97	**Versions:** Godot 4.7.2 · Blender 5.2.2 LTS · MCP for Blender add-on 1.8 (protocol 13) · Claude Code 2.1.299 (Opus 5.5) · Windows 11.
98	
99	### Rebuild, export, import, check (Windows, Git Bash, from the repo root)
100	
101	```bash
102	# Rebuild one asset from scratch in background Blender and check it (exit 0 = pass)
103	"/d/blender/blender.exe" -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python tools/blender/build_cover_wall.py
104	# (same for build_ammo_crate.py and build_tank_hedgehog.py)
105	
106	# Export one .blend to .glb (one asset per call)
107	"/d/blender/blender.exe" -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 design/blender/cover_wall.blend --python tools/blender/export_glb.py -- assets/models/cover_wall.glb
108	
109	# Godot: import, then the headless asset check (exit 0 = all pass, 1 = any FAIL, 124 = time limit hit)
110	GODOT="/d/CSYE7270/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe"
111	"$GODOT" --headless --path . --import
112	timeout 120 "$GODOT" --headless --path . --script res://tests/check_a3_assets.gd --fixed-fps 60
113	```
114	
115	`timeout` is Git Bash's GNU `timeout`; Windows' own `timeout.exe` only waits and does not stop a program. To look at the assets, open the project in Godot 4.7 and open **`scenes/asset_room_3d.tscn`**.
116	
117	### Known limitations (A3)
118	
119	- The Blender build scripts check material slot names, not colour values, and say nothing about the asset after export.
120	- The Godot check measures each `.glb` on its own at the origin. It does not check the copies placed in `asset_room_3d.tscn`, colours, lighting, shadows or whether the shapes read correctly; I checked those by eye in the editor.
121	- With one light and no ambient fill, faces turned away from the light are very dark; how the colours look under the game's real lighting is not tested.
122	- Each asset is overlapping boxes, so hidden inside faces still count towards the 36 triangles.
123	- tank_hedgehog's "apply rotation" build step had no real rotation to apply (already baked during the join), so that step is untested.
124	- ammo_crate is 1.24 × 0.84 × 0.71 m, not the brief's 1.2 × 0.8 × 0.7, because the lid overhang and stripe were left out of the brief; it is inside the ±0.1 m tolerance.
125	- The cover_wall hand edit overshoots by 0.032 mm, inside the build check's 0.1 mm tolerance.
126	- The film shows my Blender session as my own screenshots (stills), not a screen recording, and the Godot scene with a static camera.
127	- The film shows Claude's plan and report but not the text of my prompt (my screenshots do not include it). In its last second the toolkit's locked outro mascot overlaps the @NikBearBrown handle.
128	
129	Full details: [TEST-REPORT](TEST-REPORT.md) · [BLENDER-NOTES](BLENDER-NOTES.md) · [CHANGE-BRIEF](CHANGE-BRIEF.md) · [FRICTIONAL](FRICTIONAL.md) · [SOURCES](SOURCES.md). The Assignment 2 test report is in [docs/a2/TEST-REPORT.md](docs/a2/TEST-REPORT.md).
130	
131	---
132	
133	## Assignment 2
134	
135	A tank-battle asset slice for CSYE7270 Assignment 2. You drive **YunqiZ**, a worn olive tank with a dozer blade and a white identification stripe, through a ruined brick battlefield: hide behind cover that breaks under fire, pick your moment, and destroy all three enemy tanks.
136	
137	- **Started from:** an empty Godot 4 project (see [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md)).
138	- **Engine:** Godot 4.7.2 stable.
139	- **Film:** [Watch on Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1wZdhVj9YaA1GIYIu9yU09Xp2JRoVltxk/view?usp=drive_link) — `claude-liam-walker-tank-gamedev.mp4` (3840×2160 landscape), SHA-256 `b13a75400f8405be572142c3ab1c4565d49f980c2c82b4a6851c6b8d074fd150`
140	
141	## Run
142	
143	1. Open Godot 4.7, **Import** → select `project.godot` in this folder → open.
144	2. Press **F5**.
145	
146	Automated sound-trigger check (after opening the project once so assets are imported):
147	
148	```bash
149	godot --headless --path . -s res://tests/test_sound_triggers.gd
150	```
151	
152	## Controls
153	
154	| Input | Action |
155	|---|---|
156	| WASD / arrow keys | Move (the hull faces the movement direction) |
157	| Mouse | Aim the turret |
158	| Left mouse button / Space | Fire (0.8 s reload) |
159	| Esc / P | Pause |
160	| **M** | Mute / unmute music |
161	| **N** | Mute / unmute sound effects |
162	| R | Play again after victory |
163	
164	Music and sound are also toggled with the buttons at the top right.
165	
166	## What the slice demonstrates
167	
168	- **Character:** YunqiZ in 8 facings (5 generated with SDXL img2img, 3 mirrored), hull and turret as separate sprites, idle and moving states, recoil, hit flash, smoke at ≤60% health and fire at ≤30%, destruction.
169	- **Environment:** a generated ground tile and brick cover in three generated stages (intact, cracked after 2 hits, broken after 4 hits; broken cover no longer blocks).
170	- **Sound:** five generated sound effects on real events — fire, cover hit, YunqiZ hit, explosion, victory — each once per event.
171	- **Music:** a generated 8-bar loop at 70 BPM; pauses with the game, cuts on failure, restarts on respawn, stops at victory.
172	- **Loop:** three enemy tanks that move and fire back; respawn at the spawn point with destroyed enemies staying destroyed; victory screen.

177	- Muzzle flash, explosions, smoke and fire are code particles, not generated art.
178	- The opening top-down zoom (storyboard panel 1) and the low-angle victory illustration (panel 8) were not built.

## Assignment 2

A tank-battle asset slice for CSYE7270 Assignment 2. You drive **YunqiZ**, a worn olive tank with a dozer blade and a white identification stripe, through a ruined brick battlefield: hide behind cover that breaks under fire, pick your moment, and destroy all three enemy tanks.

- **Started from:** an empty Godot 4 project (see [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md)).
- **Engine:** Godot 4.7.2 stable.
- **Film:** [Watch on Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1wZdhVj9YaA1GIYIu9yU09Xp2JRoVltxk/view?usp=drive_link) — `claude-liam-walker-tank-gamedev.mp4` (3840×2160 landscape), SHA-256 `b13a75400f8405be572142c3ab1c4565d49f980c2c82b4a6851c6b8d074fd150`

## Run

1. Open Godot 4.7, **Import** → select `project.godot` in this folder → open.
2. Press **F5**.

Automated sound-trigger check (after opening the project once so assets are imported):

```bash
godot --headless --path . -s res://tests/test_sound_triggers.gd
```

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| WASD / arrow keys | Move (the hull faces the movement direction) |
| Mouse | Aim the turret |
| Left mouse button / Space | Fire (0.8 s reload) |
| Esc / P | Pause |
| **M** | Mute / unmute music |
| **N** | Mute / unmute sound effects |
| R | Play again after victory |

Music and sound are also toggled with the buttons at the top right.

## What the slice demonstrates

- **Character:** YunqiZ in 8 facings (5 generated with SDXL img2img, 3 mirrored), hull and turret as separate sprites, idle and moving states, recoil, hit flash, smoke at ≤60% health and fire at ≤30%, destruction.
- **Environment:** a generated ground tile and brick cover in three generated stages (intact, cracked after 2 hits, broken after 4 hits; broken cover no longer blocks).
- **Sound:** five generated sound effects on real events — fire, cover hit, YunqiZ hit, explosion, victory — each once per event.
- **Music:** a generated 8-bar loop at 70 BPM; pauses with the game, cuts on failure, restarts on respawn, stops at victory.
- **Loop:** three enemy tanks that move and fire back; respawn at the spawn point with destroyed enemies staying destroyed; victory screen.

## Known limitations

- Enemy tanks are the YunqiZ sprites tinted grey, not separate designs.
- Muzzle flash, explosions, smoke and fire are code particles, not generated art.
- The opening top-down zoom (storyboard panel 1) and the low-angle victory illustration (panel 8) were not built.
- The up and right turrets have no commander cupola; the other three do.
- Cannon and explosion sounds are mostly low frequency and may be quiet on laptop speakers.
- The hull snaps between 8 facings and the turret could turn more responsively.

306	- **The tank_hedgehog script's "apply rotation" step tested nothing.** The beams' rotation was already baked into the mesh during the join, so the bake step found identity transforms (it printed `identity: True`). The result is correct, but that step never had a real rotation to apply.
307	- **The Godot check** measures each `.glb` on its own, instantiated at the origin: size, lowest Y, root scale and the height axis, to 0.01 m. It does **not** check the copies placed in `asset_room_3d.tscn`, whether they rest on the floor there, colours, lighting, shadows, or whether the shapes read as what they are. Headless Godot uses a dummy renderer, so none of that is visible to it.
308	- **Hidden faces:** each asset is made of overlapping boxes, so faces inside the asset (the crate lid's underside, the wall's block bottoms, the hedgehog's crossing) still count towards the 36 triangles. They are never visible, so I left them.
309	
310	## Problems found and what I changed
311	
312	1. **tank_hedgehog's brief was wrong (evidence-based revision).** I asked Claude to work out the bounding box *before* building. With the brief's 2.4 m beams it came to 2.011 × 2.011 × **1.559** m, 0.009 m over the height tolerance, because the brief's numbers used the beam centrelines and left out the 0.15 m section. Claude recommended turning each beam 45° to fit. I chose instead to shorten the beams to **2.125 m**, because the overall size is what the game design depends on (lower than the 1.6 m hull, a barrier at hull scale), while the beam length was only a construction detail and was the number that was wrong. Result: 1.794 × 1.794 × 1.400 m. The change is recorded under *Revisions* in `CHANGE-BRIEF.md`; the original text is unchanged.
313	2. **ammo_crate's brief size left out the lid.** The brief lists the body size, but the lid overhangs by 0.02 m on each side and the stripe adds 0.01 m, so the real box is 1.24 × 0.84 × 0.71 m. Inside the ±0.1 m tolerance, so I kept it; the build script checks both the exact size and the brief tolerance.
314	3. **ammo_crate z-fighting avoided.** Claude noticed before building that a stripe exactly as deep as the lid (0.84 m) would share the lid's front and back faces and could flicker. I accepted its suggestion to make the stripe 0.83 m deep. The overall size did not change.
315	4. **My hand edit on cover_wall was 0.7 mm short.** I moved block B +0.6 m in Edit Mode. My sidebar then showed 4 m wide and I thought it was flush. Claude's read-only background inspection showed it had moved 0.5993 m, 0.7 mm short: **the sidebar rounds, so it could not show that error.** My correction (G X 0.0007, computed from a 4-decimal printout that was itself rounded) overshot by 0.032 mm. That is inside the build check's 0.1 mm tolerance and far below anything visible, so I stopped there. Lesson: to place something exactly, type the coordinate into the sidebar instead of nudging with G; and decide the tolerance first, then stop when inside it.
316	
317	## HUMAN CHECK: look
318	
319	*My own observations in the Godot editor (`scenes/asset_room_3d.tscn`), with the grey 6.0 × 1.6 × 3.4 m box standing in for the YunqiZ hull. Screenshot: `design/godot/asset_room_3d.png`.*
320	
321	- **From the top** (the game's camera direction): the ammo crate's off-white stripe is the most readable feature in the scene, which is what the brief wanted. The hedgehog reads as three crossing beams. The wall's shadow shows its broken top, higher on the left.
322	- **Floor contact:** every asset casts a shadow that meets its base; none of them floats. (This is the check the headless script cannot do for the scene copies.)
323	- **Scale:** next to the hull box, the wall is wider than the hull is deep and lower than the turret would be, the crate is small enough to drive over, and the hedgehog is clearly lower than the hull. All three look in proportion.
324	- **From behind and below:** I switched the editor to the rear and bottom views for each asset. I saw no missing faces and no wrong colours; I found no problems to fix.
325	- **Not resolved:** with one light and no ambient fill, faces turned away from the light are very dark. The brief asked for one light; whether the game's real lighting suits these colours is not tested here.
326	
327	## Brief failure cases, predicted vs. what happened
328	
329	| # | Predicted | What happened |
330	|---|---|---|
331	| 1 | Lying on its side (Z-up vs Y-up) | Did not happen; height is on Godot Y for all three |
332	| 2 | Scale or rotation not applied | Did not happen; scale 1, 1, 1 in Blender and Godot. Building from mesh data meant scale was never non-1 |
333	| 3 | Origin in the middle, floats or sinks | Did not happen; lowest Y 0.0000 in Godot |
334	| 4 | Claude builds more than asked | Did not happen; 36 triangles each, 3 boxes each |
335	| 5 | Colours lost on export | Did not happen; colours visible in the Godot screenshot (checked by eye, not measured) |
336	| 6 | MCP will not connect on Windows | Connected, after one failed command (see FRICTIONAL.md) |
337	
338	Not predicted: the hedgehog's brief size being wrong, the crate's lid overhang, and a Blender error (`AttributeError ... 'select_set'`) during cover_wall's join.
339

## Rerun at `3d48047` (2026-10-27), one command per call

| Command | Result | Exit | Log |
|---|---|---|---|

None of the seven logs contains `SHADER ERROR` or `SCRIPT ERROR`. At shutdown, `test_hit_flash` prints "13 / 16 / 14 ObjectDB instances were leaked" (at 30 / 60 / 144) and "5 resources still in use at exit". `test_sound_triggers` prints "22 ObjectDB instances" and "7 resources still in use". These are engine shutdown messages, not test failures (see Baseline).

---

## 1. Baseline (before and after)

| | `check_a3_assets.gd` @ 60 | `test_sound_triggers.gd` @ 60 |
|---|---|---|
| **Before A5** (commit `c4a1f84`, brief line 9) | 18/18 PASS, exit 0 | 8/8 PASS, exit 0, with "5 resources still in use at exit" |
| After Step 2 (`9217896`, [docs/a5/step2-output.txt](docs/a5/step2-output.txt)) | 18/18, exit 0 | 8/8, exit 0 (log: 18 ObjectDB, 5 resources) |
| After Step 3 (`97fdec6`, [docs/a5/step3-finish-b.txt](docs/a5/step3-finish-b.txt)) | 18/18, exit 0 | 8/8, exit 0 (log: 22 ObjectDB, 7 resources) |
| **After A5** (this rerun at `3d48047`) | **18/18 PASS, exit 0** | **8/8 PASS, exit 0** (22 ObjectDB, 7 resources) |

The pass counts are unchanged and neither test file was edited. **Finding:** Recorded, not investigated: the shutdown message grew from 5 resources / 18 ObjectDB instances to 7 / 22 between `9217896` and `97fdec6`. It is not a SHADER or SCRIPT ERROR and the 8/8 result is unchanged.

## 2. Shaders parse

From `tests/test_hit_flash.gd` (all three rates, identical lines) and `tests/test_materials.gd`:

- `hit_flash.gdshader` loads, and `get_shader_uniform_list()` is non-empty, so the shader compiled. It reports `hit_amount` (type 3 float, hint 1 range `0.0,1.0,0.001`), `flash_color` (type 20 Color, hint 0) and `flash_strength` (float, range `0.0,1.0,0.001`).
- `source_color` is not visible in the uniform list (it reports the vec4 as a Color with hint 0), so the test checks it from the source text: `flash_color vec4 source_color = vec4(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)`, `hit_amount ... = 0.0`, `flash_strength ... = 0.6`, `shader_type canvas_item`. All PASS.
- "shader declares every uniform the driver sets: hit_amount" PASS.
- `brick_surface.gdshader`: compiled, 6 uniforms, every source uniform in the compiled list. `hint_experiment.gdshader`: compiled, `render_mode unshaded`. All PASS ([logs/test_materials_60fps.log](logs/test_materials_60fps.log)).
- No `SHADER ERROR` in any of the seven logs.

**Mutations.** I made each mutation by hand, ran the test, then restored the file (restore diff empty). Output: [docs/a5/step2-output.txt](docs/a5/step2-output.txt) sections 3a and 3b.

| # | Mutation in `shaders/hit_flash.gdshader` | What the log shows | Exit | Log |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | delete the `;` after `flash_strength ... = 0.6` (line 5) | `SHADER ERROR: Expected a ';'.`, `ERROR: Shader compilation failed.`, 5 FAILs (uniform list empty, the three uniforms, driver-uniform check); `RESULT: 45 passed, 5 failed` | **1** | [logs/mutation1_semicolon_60fps.log](logs/mutation1_semicolon_60fps.log) |
| 2 | rename `hit_amount` → `hit_amt` (lines 3 and 8) | no shader error (the shader is valid). The driver prints `ERROR: hit_flash_driver: ... does not declare uniform 'hit_amount'`; 3 FAILs; `RESULT: 47 passed, 3 failed` | **1** | [logs/mutation2_rename_60fps.log](logs/mutation2_rename_60fps.log) |

Mutation 1 settled a question the agent could not answer in session 2: headless does report shader parse errors. Mutation 2 is brief failure case 5: `set_shader_parameter` on an undeclared name raises no error by itself. Here the driver's own check printed an `ERROR:` line and the uniform-list assertions failed, but that `ERROR:` line alone would not make the wrapper exit 1 (it only looks for `SHADER ERROR` / `SCRIPT ERROR`). The exit 1 comes from the test's FAILs.

## 3. Driver (`scripts/hit_flash_driver.gd`, attached in `scripts/main.gd` by one line)

`tests/test_hit_flash.gd` runs the real game loop and samples `hit_amount` every frame from a high-`process_priority` node. Results are the same at all three rates (50/50 each):

| Check (brief rule) | 30 fps | 60 fps | 144 fps |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before any hit | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| **Real shell hit:** enemy `try_fire()` spawns a shell that hits YunqiZ (`damaged` emitted, health 75) | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| Existing white `_flash()` still runs (modulate 2.2 at the signal) | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| Rule 1: **first** sampled frame after the hit | **1.0** | **1.0** | **1.0** |
| Rule 2: falls linearly on game time (1 − t/D) | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| Rule 2: **last** value 0.0, reached after **0.5000 s** game time (tolerance ± one frame) | 0.5000 s (± 0.0333) | 0.5000 s (± 0.0167) | 0.5000 s (± 0.0069) |
| Rule 2: stays 0.0 afterwards | 12 frames | 24 frames | 58 frames |
| Rule 5: pause mid-fade, value before pause | 0.6667 | 0.6333 | 0.6111 |
| Rule 5: holds on all 12 paused frames, falls again after unpause | 0.6667 → 0.5333 | 0.6333 → 0.5667 | 0.6111 → 0.5833 |
| Rule 3: **retrigger** lands after invulnerability | at 0.400 s (value before 0.2667) | at 0.400 s (0.2333) | at 0.403 s (0.2083) |
| Rule 3: first frame after retrigger | 1.0 | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| Rule 6: fatal hit → `destroyed`, no `damaged`; first frame after | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| Rule 6: 0.0 on every frame from `destroyed` through `reset_full()` (health 100) | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| Second retrigger after respawn restarts at 1.0, then full fade 0.5000 s | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| Rule 7: hull has the ShaderMaterial; hull and turret return the same material object; no enemy sprite has a ShaderMaterial (checked at start and end) | PASS | PASS | PASS |

Rule 4 (scaled time): the fade lasts the same 0.5000 s of game time at 30, 60 and 144 fps, so the driver does not count frames (brief failure case 2). Nothing in the project changes `Engine.time_scale`, so no run had a time scale other than 1.

Known limit (from the session-2 report, in my notes): `reset_full()` on a *living* tank mid-fade would not clear the value. The game only calls it after death, and rule 6 covers that path.

## 4. Controlled values — HUMAN CHECK

**How captured:** `tools/capture_hit_flash.gd` (written by Claude Code, session 5). I ran it windowed at 1280×720. It freezes the enemies, faces YunqiZ right (slot 0, `hull_right.png`, no flip, modulate = tint = (1,1,1)), stops the driver, sets `hit_amount`, waits for the frame to be drawn, saves `get_viewport().get_texture().get_image()`, and reads the value back. Printed output: [docs/a5/captures-output.txt](docs/a5/captures-output.txt). CSV: [docs/a5/captures/hit_flash_pixels.csv](docs/a5/captures/hit_flash_pixels.csv). Captures: [hit_flash_0.0.png](docs/a5/captures/hit_flash_0.0.png), [hit_flash_0.5.png](docs/a5/captures/hit_flash_0.5.png), [hit_flash_1.0.png](docs/a5/captures/hit_flash_1.0.png), [hit_flash_2.0.png](docs/a5/captures/hit_flash_2.0.png).

P1 = hull texel (99, 50), screen (155, 590). P2 = hull texel (59, 109), screen (135, 620). The table shows measured centre pixels; the 3×3 screen mean is in the CSV. Tolerance (brief §3): ±2 per channel.

| `hit_amount` | P1 predicted (hull) | P1 measured | max diff | P2 predicted | P2 measured | max diff |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0 | (87, 97, 40) | (70, 76, 31) | **21** | (16, 16, 16) | (16, 16, 16) | **0** |
| 0.5 | (137, 68, 28) | (126, 53, 22) | **15** | (88, 11, 11) | (88, 11, 11) | **0** |
| 1.0 | (188, 39, 16) | (181, 31, 12) | **8** | (159, 6, 6) | (159, 6, 6) | **0** |

- **P2 matches exactly** at all three values.
- **P1 does not match the hull prediction.** The tool reports turret alpha 1.00 over P1: the **turret sprite covers that pixel**. See *Inspect-and-revise cycle* below.
- **Recomputed turret values** (CHANGE-BRIEF *Revision* 2026-10-27, computed **after** the observation, so not a prediction). Turret texel `turret_right.png` (99, 71) = (70, 76, 31), alpha 252, read with PIL ([docs/a5/use-it-part2.txt](docs/a5/use-it-part2.txt) section 3):

  | `hit_amount` | turret recomputed | measured | max diff |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 0.0 | (70, 76, 31) | (70, 76, 31) | 0 |
  | 0.5 | (126, 53, 22) | (126, 53, 22) | 0 |
  | 1.0 | (181, 30, 12) | (181, 31, 12) | 1 |

- **2.0 capture and the hint_range answer:** with `hit_amount = 2.0` set from code (read back as 2.0 after saving), both P1 and P2 are **(255, 0, 0)**. The brief §7 prediction was that `hint_range` does not clamp a value set from code. **Confirmed:** at 1.0 the pixels are still well inside the range, and at 2.0 (t = 1.2) the mix extrapolates past red and the display clips to (255, 0, 0). `hint_range` shapes only the Inspector slider.
- **Which capture I trust, and why.** I trust the engine capture (`get_viewport().get_texture().get_image()`) for measurement. From the sources: it is the 1280×720 viewport image itself, taken in the frame after the value was set, and the tool read the value back after saving. I also tried OS screenshots. The first captured the wrong window (an 850×287 terminal screenshot). The second (1920×1080, Win+PrtScn) showed the same values (my notes record this for the six hint bands). My notes record the choice without a further reason. The OS screenshot files are not in the repo: TBD.

## 5. In play — HUMAN CHECK

My playtest (2026-10-27, in the editor), verbatim from my notes:

> Got hit several times by enemy shells. Each hit flashed YunqiZ red and faded quickly; a second hit during the fade restarted it. Enemies hit by my shells did not flash red (only their existing white flash and the impact effect). After being destroyed and respawning there was no red left. I did not see the existing white flash on YunqiZ: the test shows modulate still reaches 2.2, but at the same moment the red is at its strongest. I tried to pause with Esc during the fade but could not press it within 0.5 s, so rule 5 rests on the headless test only.

Playtesters other than me: none recorded. Captures or video of the playtest: TBD.

## 6. Hint experiment — HUMAN CHECK

`tools/capture_hint.gd`, run windowed by me. Capture: [docs/a5/captures/hint_both.png](docs/a5/captures/hint_both.png). CSV: [docs/a5/captures/hint_pixels.csv](docs/a5/captures/hint_pixels.csv). Scene `scenes/hint_experiment.tscn` (Linear tonemap, exposure 1.0, glow/fog/adjustments off, unshaded). Tool output: [docs/a5/captures-output.txt](docs/a5/captures-output.txt).

| Band (file value) | Quad A `hint_srgb` (with `source_color`): predicted | measured | Quad B `hint_raw` (without): predicted | measured |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 64 | **64** | 137 | **137** |
| 128 | 128 | **128** | 188 | **188** |
| 192 | 192 | **192** | 225 | **225** |

All six bands match exactly, centre and 3×3 mean (difference 0). Quad A shows the file's values because the sRGB decode at the sample and the encode at the output cancel. Quad B is brighter because the stored value is treated as linear and still encoded. My 1920×1080 OS screenshot showed the same six values (my notes).

## 7. Interface sweep — HUMAN CHECK

`tools/capture_materials.gd`, run windowed by me on `materials/cover_wall_intact.tres` as loaded on CoverWall; the damaged wall was untouched. Values are the mean RGB of an 11×11 px box on the front face at (334, 371); CoverWall2's box at (134, 371) stays at (49.9, 36.1, 27.1) in every sweep capture. CSV: [docs/a5/captures/materials_captures.csv](docs/a5/captures/materials_captures.csv). Output: [docs/a5/captures-output.txt](docs/a5/captures-output.txt). Light: the scene's only light, `Sun` (DirectionalLight3D, shadows on), no WorldEnvironment ([MATERIALS.md](MATERIALS.md) §4).

**I am describing these images from the numbers only.** Where my notes say nothing about the look, it is marked *to confirm by eye*.

| Uniform | Step | Value | CoverWall mean RGB | Capture |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `albedo_tint` | min | (0, 0, 0, 1) | (22.1, 22.1, 22.1) | [sweep_albedo_tint_min.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_albedo_tint_min.png) |
| | default | (1, 1, 1, 1) | (73.4, 54.1, 37.7) | [sweep_albedo_tint_default.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_albedo_tint_default.png) |
| | max (= default) | (1, 1, 1, 1) | (73.4, 54.1, 37.7) | [sweep_albedo_tint_max.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_albedo_tint_max.png) |
| `brightness` | min | 0.0 | (22.1, 22.1, 22.1) | [sweep_brightness_min.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_brightness_min.png) |
| | default | 1.0 | (73.4, 54.1, 37.7) | [sweep_brightness_default.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_brightness_default.png) |
| | max | 2.0 | (99.7, 72.7, 48.5) | [sweep_brightness_max.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_brightness_max.png) |
| `roughness_scale` | min | 0.0 | (68.8, 47.4, 26.9) | [sweep_roughness_scale_min.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_roughness_scale_min.png) |
| | default | 1.0 | (73.4, 54.1, 37.7) | [sweep_roughness_scale_default.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_roughness_scale_default.png) |
| | max (= default) | 1.0 | (73.4, 54.1, 37.7) | [sweep_roughness_scale_max.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_roughness_scale_max.png) |
| `uv_scale` | min | 0.1 | (76.8, 52.0, 34.4) | [sweep_uv_scale_min.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_uv_scale_min.png) |
| | default | 0.5 | (73.4, 54.1, 37.7) | [sweep_uv_scale_default.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_uv_scale_default.png) |
| | max | 4.0 | (79.8, 52.7, 33.1) | [sweep_uv_scale_max.png](docs/a5/captures/sweep_uv_scale_max.png) |

What changed, uniform by uniform:

- **`albedo_tint`.** Black gives (22.1, 22.1, 22.1), **not black**. My notes: "specular/ambient remain". The default and maximum are the same value, so the sweep has only one real step. The look of a coloured tint (brief: "darker or warmer tints recolour them") was not captured: TBD.
- **`brightness`.** 0 gives the same (22.1, 22.1, 22.1) as a black tint, again not black. At 2 the mean rises from 73.4 to 99.7 on R, not to 146. # TEST-REPORT — Assignment 3: three 3D assets

The Assignment 2 report has moved, unchanged, to `docs/a2/TEST-REPORT.md`.

**Versions:** Blender 5.2.2 LTS · MCP for Blender add-on 1.8 (protocol 13) · Godot 4.7.2 · Claude Code 2.1.299 (Opus 5.5) · Windows 11, RTX 3060 laptop.

**How to re-run the checks (Windows, Git Bash, from the repo root):**

```bash
# Blender: rebuild each asset from scratch and check it (exit 0 = pass)
"/d/blender/blender.exe" -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python tools/blender/build_cover_wall.py
# (same for build_ammo_crate.py and build_tank_hedgehog.py)

# Godot: import, then the headless asset check (exit 0 = all pass, 1 = any FAIL, 124 = time limit hit)
GODOT="/d/CSYE7270/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe"
"$GODOT" --headless --path . --import
timeout 120 "$GODOT" --headless --path . --script res://tests/check_a3_assets.gd --fixed-fps 60
```

The course commands are written for macOS. On Windows I use Git Bash's GNU `timeout` (coreutils 8.32), because Windows' own `timeout.exe` only waits and does not stop a program; and `--path .` because my Godot project is the repo root, not a `godot/` folder.

## Results

All sizes in metres. Blender is Z-up, Godot is Y-up, so a Blender (x, y, z) size appears in Godot as (x, z, y).

| Check | cover_wall | ammo_crate | tank_hedgehog |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Brief** (w × d × h) | 4.0 × 1.0 × 1.8 | 1.2 × 0.8 × 0.7 (±0.1) | about 1.9 × 1.9 × 1.4 (±0.15) |
| **Blender** (x × y × z; build-script check; my sidebar for cover_wall) | 4.0 × 1.0 × 1.8 | 1.24 × 0.84 × 0.71 | 1.794 × 1.794 × 1.400 |
| **Godot headless** (x × y × z) | 4.000032 × 1.8 × 1.0 | 1.24 × 0.71 × 0.84 | 1.794236 × 1.400074 × 1.794236 |
| Matches brief? | yes | yes, +0.04 / +0.04 / +0.01, inside ±0.1 | yes after the revision below; height exact |
| **Upright** (height on Godot Y) | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| **Root node scale** in Godot | 1, 1, 1 | 1, 1, 1 | 1, 1, 1 |
| **Lowest Y** in Godot (origin on floor) | 0.0000 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 (3 vertices at Blender Z = 0) |
| **Triangles** (budget 60) | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| **Background rebuild** in Blender | exit 0 | exit 0 | exit 0 |
| **Godot check** overall | 18 / 18 PASS, exit 0 | | |

Every number above comes from a script output I kept (Blender build-script runs, and `tests/check_a3_assets.gd`, commit `ee1c67a`).

## The check failing on purpose

A check that has never failed may be broken. Claude ran a scratch copy of `check_a3_assets.gd` whose only difference (confirmed with `diff`) was ammo_crate's expected height changed from 0.71 to 0.81. It printed two FAIL lines and `RESULT: FAIL (2 failure(s))` with **exit code 1**; the other 16 checks still passed. The real script and the assets were not changed.

## What the checks do and do not show

- **The Blender build scripts** show that each asset can be rebuilt from nothing with the stated size, origin, applied transforms, triangle count and material slot *names*. They do not check colour values, and they say nothing about the asset after export.
- **The tank_hedgehog script's "apply rotation" step tested nothing.** The beams' rotation was already baked into the mesh during the join, so the bake step found identity transforms (it printed `identity: True`). The result is correct, but that step never had a real rotation to apply.
- **The Godot check** measures each `.glb` on its own, instantiated at the origin: size, lowest Y, root scale and the height axis, to 0.01 m. It does **not** check the copies placed in `asset_room_3d.tscn`, whether they rest on the floor there, colours, lighting, shadows, or whether the shapes read as what they are. Headless Godot uses a dummy renderer, so none of that is visible to it.
- **Hidden faces:** each asset is made of overlapping boxes, so faces inside the asset (the crate lid's underside, the wall's block bottoms, the hedgehog's crossing) still count towards the 36 triangles. They are never visible, so I left them.

## Problems found and what I changed

1. **tank_hedgehog's brief was wrong (evidence-based revision).** I asked Claude to work out the bounding box *before* building. With the brief's 2.4 m beams it came to 2.011 × 2.011 × **1.559** m, 0.009 m over the height tolerance, because the brief's numbers used the beam centrelines and left out the 0.15 m section. Claude recommended turning each beam 45° to fit. I chose instead to shorten the beams to **2.125 m**, because the overall size is what the game design depends on (lower than the 1.6 m hull, a barrier at hull scale), while the beam length was only a construction detail and was the number that was wrong. Result: 1.794 × 1.794 × 1.400 m. The change is recorded under *Revisions* in `CHANGE-BRIEF.md`; the original text is unchanged.
2. **ammo_crate's brief size left out the lid.** The brief lists the body size, but the lid overhangs by 0.02 m on each side and the stripe adds 0.01 m, so the real box is 1.24 × 0.84 × 0.71 m. Inside the ±0.1 m tolerance, so I kept it; the build script checks both the exact size and the brief tolerance.
3. **ammo_crate z-fighting avoided.** Claude noticed before building that a stripe exactly as deep as the lid (0.84 m) would share the lid's front and back faces and could flicker. I accepted its suggestion to make the stripe 0.83 m deep. The overall size did not change.
4. **My hand edit on cover_wall was 0.7 mm short.** I moved block B +0.6 m in Edit Mode. My sidebar then showed 4 m wide and I thought it was flush. Claude's read-only background inspection showed it had moved 0.5993 m, 0.7 mm short: **the sidebar rounds, so it could not show that error.** My correction (G X 0.0007, computed from a 4-decimal printout that was itself rounded) overshot by 0.032 mm. That is inside the build check's 0.1 mm tolerance and far below anything visible, so I stopped there. Lesson: to place something exactly, type the coordinate into the sidebar instead of nudging with G; and decide the tolerance first, then stop when inside it.

## HUMAN CHECK: look

*My own observations in the Godot editor (`scenes/asset_room_3d.tscn`), with the grey 6.0 × 1.6 × 3.4 m box standing in for the YunqiZ hull. Screenshot: `design/godot/asset_room_3d.png`.*

- **From the top** (the game's camera direction): the ammo crate's off-white stripe is the most readable feature in the scene, which is what the brief wanted. The hedgehog reads as three crossing beams. The wall's shadow shows its broken top, higher on the left.
- **Floor contact:** every asset casts a shadow that meets its base; none of them floats. (This is the check the headless script cannot do for the scene copies.)
- **Scale:** next to the hull box, the wall is wider than the hull is deep and lower than the turret would be, the crate is small enough to drive over, and the hedgehog is clearly lower than the hull. All three look in proportion.
- **From behind and below:** I switched the editor to the rear and bottom views for each asset. I saw no missing faces and no wrong colours; I found no problems to fix.
- **Not resolved:** with one light and no ambient fill, faces turned away from the light are very dark. The brief asked for one light; whether the game's real lighting suits these colours is not tested here.

## Brief failure cases, predicted vs. what happened

| # | Predicted | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lying on its side (Z-up vs Y-up) | Did not happen; height is on Godot Y for all three |
| 2 | Scale or rotation not applied | Did not happen; scale 1, 1, 1 in Blender and Godot. Building from mesh data meant scale was never non-1 |
| 3 | Origin in the middle, floats or sinks | Did not happen; lowest Y 0.0000 in Godot |
| 4 | Claude builds more than asked | Did not happen; 36 triangles each, 3 boxes each |
| 5 | Colours lost on export | Did not happen; colours visible in the Godot screenshot (checked by eye, not measured) |
| 6 | MCP will not connect on Windows | Connected, after one failed command (see FRICTIONAL.md) |

Not predicted: the hedgehog's brief size being wrong, the crate's lid overhang, and a Blender error (`AttributeError ... 'select_set'`) during cover_wall's join.

# Assignment 5 — hit flash shader and brick surface materials

**How this was written.** I kept raw notes in order while working ([docs/a5/frictional-notes.md](docs/a5/frictional-notes.md), commit `3d48047`; organised from my session with Claude chat and reviewed by me). Claude Code (session 6, [docs/a5/sessions/prompt-6.txt](docs/a5/sessions/prompt-6.txt)) arranged them into the dated entries below. It added only commit hashes, file paths, log and capture names and numbers taken from those files. The wording is mine where possible. **Retrospective:** every entry was written from my notes on 2026-10-27. The 2026-10-25 setup entry was written two days after the work; the others on the same day.

- **What and why:** on cover_wall, I selected the lower top block (block B) in Edit Mode with L and moved it +0.6 m along X (G X 0.6), so it is flush with the right end. From the game's top-down camera, two broken stubs with a gap in the middle read more like a shell-damaged wall than one block in the middle.
- **What it taught me:** moving part of a joined mesh in Edit Mode changes only the vertices; the object's location, rotation and scale stayed 0 / 0 / 1, so the origin stayed on the floor and nothing needed re-applying. In the front view the block looked as if it stuck out past the wall; my sidebar said 4 m, so I trusted the number over my eye.
- **But the sidebar was not precise enough.** Claude's read-only background inspection of the saved file showed block B had moved 0.5993 m, 0.7 mm short; the sidebar rounds to display precision, so it could not show this. I corrected by hand (G X 0.0007), computed from a 4-decimal printout that was itself rounded, so it then overshot by 0.032 mm. That is inside the build check's 0.1 mm tolerance and far below anything visible, so I stopped. Next time I would type the target coordinate into the sidebar instead of nudging with G.
- Claude added the edit to `build_cover_wall.py` as a separate, clearly labelled step 7, so the script rebuilds the final asset. Commit `4846465`.
- **Two process slips here.** (1) While doing this I found Claude Code had switched back to **auto mode**: the script append and a background run were "Allowed by auto mode classifier" without my approval. Nothing harmful ran, but I only noticed afterwards; I switched back to manual mode. (2) Claude then wanted to run a temporary inspection script I could not see. I refused, asked to see its full contents, checked it had no save or export calls, and only then approved it.

The crate's stripe is the most readable feature from above; the hedgehog reads as crossing beams; every shadow meets its asset's base; I saw no missing faces or wrong colours. # FRICTIONAL — walker-TANK

How the design went, in order. **Retrospective note:** this log was put together on 2026-10-05 from my chat with Claude, the settings ComfyUI saved inside each output file, my screenshots and the commits. Claude organized it; the decisions and the reasons quoted are mine from that chat. Asset-log rows are in [ASSET-LOG.md](ASSET-LOG.md).

**Who is who:** *Me* = what I chose, ran, judged or changed. *Claude* = the AI assistant (plans, prompts, code, scripts, guide images, drafts). *Model* = the generative model that made the asset (SDXL Base 1.0, Stable Audio 3 Small).

---

## 2026-10-02 — choosing the game

- **Wanted:** a game I could keep building this semester.
- **Asked:** Claude to compare two ideas I had, a tank battle and a farm fruit-picking game, against the assignment rules.
- **Got:** Claude said the tank game had natural sound events and was easier to keep consistent, but hard to get 10 poses from a vehicle; the farm game had easy poses but no built-in way to fail.
- **Decided:** tank battle. Then I chose: clear all enemy tanks, oblique top-down view, realistic metal look, cover that breaks, a health bar, about 5 minutes per level, all four suggested pillars, one music loop that stops on pause, failure and the end.
- **Human / Claude / model:** I made each choice from options Claude listed. Claude wrote CONCEPT.md from my answers.
- **Trace:** CONCEPT.md; first design commit.

## 2026-10-02 — silhouette test changes the tank

- **Wanted:** the player to see which way the tank faces at game size.
- **Got:** Claude drew a box-model tank in 5 directions. At 64 px, **up and down looked the same**; only the barrel was different.
- **Decided:** I added a **front dozer blade** and a **rear storage box** to the design. The redrawn silhouette shows a wide bar at the front.
- **Human / Claude / model:** I chose the blade and the box. Claude drew the sketches with code (not a generative model).
- **Trace:** CHARACTER-SHEET.md (silhouette section); `design/character/silhouette.png`.

## 2026-10-02 — hull, first try: flat blocks

- **Wanted:** a realistic worn steel hull that keeps the same shape in all 5 directions.
- **Asked:** SDXL Base 1.0 img2img on Claude's box guide (v1), seed 846322750311363, 25 steps, cfg 7.0, prompt "realistic military tank hull without turret, …".
- **Got:** at denoise **0.55** and **0.70**, almost the same flat color blocks as the guide. At **0.80** some panel lines appeared, but **the dozer blade disappeared**.
- **Decided:** rejected all three. The problem was the guide, not the denoise: flat colors with black outlines read as a flat drawing.
- **Next:** Claude redrew the guide (v2) with shading, grain, road wheels and panel lines.
- **Human / Claude / model:** I ran the tests and changed only the denoise each time, so the results could be compared. Claude found the cause and made v2.
- **Trace:** ASSET-LOG G-01 to G-03; thumbnails REJ-01 to REJ-03.

## 2026-10-02 — hull, second try: it works

- **Asked:** same seed and prompt, v2 guide, denoise 0.55 and 0.65.
- **Got:** 0.55 gave worn olive paint, rust, wheels and a segmented blade, **with the shape kept**. 0.65 looked richer but **added a turret dome on the hull**.
- **Decided:** accepted 0.55 for all 5 directions; rejected 0.65 because the turret is a separate sprite, so the tank would have two turrets.
- **Got (5 directions):** all outlines matched the guides (IoU 0.99). The down hull was brighter and the down-right hull less worn.
- **Human / Claude / model:** I ran all 5 and uploaded them. Claude checked them, cut out the backgrounds and drafted the log; I reviewed it.
- **Mistake caught:** Claude's first cutout script dropped the dozer blade on the right hull (it is a separate piece). Found on the check sheet and fixed.
- **Trace:** ASSET-LOG G-04 to G-10; `design/asset-log/check_hull_v2.png`.

## 2026-10-02 — turret: square barrel vs round barrel

- **Got:** with the v2 guide, the right turret had a **square** barrel and the down-right one a **round** barrel.
- **Decided:** I asked to fix this **before** running the other directions. Claude suggested the round barrel (like the down-right one) and I agreed. Claude drew a v3 guide with a round barrel and muzzle.
- **Also:** twice I loaded one guide and saved under another direction's name, so I had to rename files.
- **Trace:** ASSET-LOG T-01, T-02; REJ-05, REJ-06.

## 2026-10-02 — turret denoise: 0.55, 0.60 or 0.75

- **Got:** 0.55 nearly lost the hatch. 0.60 gave a raised domed cupola. 0.75 gave a round turret with a gun mantle and muzzle brake.
- **Decided:** I said "0.60 looks better than 0.55", then "0.75 is even better". Claude pointed out that 0.75 **lost the white stripe**, changed the turret shape and the barrel color. I chose **0.60**.
- **Human / Claude / model:** the first preference (0.75) was mine; Claude raised the problems; the final choice (0.60) was mine.
- **Trace:** ASSET-LOG T-03 to T-05; REJ-07, REJ-08.

## 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-04 — the cupola only appeared on some turrets

- **Got:** at 0.60, the diagonal turrets had a cupola but up, right and down had flat tops. The down turret also lost the stripe and had a clamp on the barrel.
- **Decided:** I chose to **re-run up, right and down until they had a cupola**. Claude made a v3.1 guide with a bigger cupola and a stronger prompt. The stripe would be painted on every turret afterwards so it is the same everywhere.
- **Got:** down was still flat with the same seed. With random seeds one had a cupola but a light barrel. The one I finally kept was made with denoise 0.55 on the v3.1 guide, seed 499619143762383 (these settings are read from the file itself): cupola, dark barrel, no clamp.
- **Decided:** after that I said "never mind, I don't want to keep changing it". Up and right stay flat. At game size the difference is 1–2 px.

## 2026-10-04 — stripe and color fixes (edits)

- **Edits:** Claude's script painted the white stripe where the guide puts it on all 5 turrets, and matched the olive of all 10 sprites to the sheet color `#4B5320`.
- **Trace:** ASSET-LOG Edits; `design/asset-log/check_stripe_before_after.png`.

## 2026-10-05 — cannon sound: the template's settings were wrong

- **Wanted:** a deep, heavy cannon shot (pillar: every shot has weight).
- **Asked:** Stable Audio 3 Small-SFX, prompt "single heavy tank cannon shot, deep low boom with a sharp crack, …".
- **Got:** seven noisy bursts in 2 seconds, clipping, no decay. Claude read the settings saved in the FLAC file: 50 steps and cfg 7.0, which the template sets for the bigger Medium model.
- **Next:** I changed the sampler to 8 steps / cfg 1.0. The new shot was one clean low boom that fades out.
- **Trace:** ASSET-LOG A-01, A-02; `design/asset-log/audio/SFX-fire_waveforms.png`.

## 2026-10-05 — other sounds and music

- **Got:** cover hit, YunqiZ hit, victory and the music loop were usable on the first try. Claude checked each one's length, frequency spread and clipping. The music came out at exactly 70 BPM; Claude cut an 8-bar loop and I played the game with it.
- **Decided:** Claude warned that the cannon and the explosion are both almost all low frequency, so they sound alike and may be quiet on laptop speakers. I said "leave it, I'm short on time."
- **Still unresolved:** the cannon and explosion sounds.
- **Trace:** ASSET-LOG A-03 to A-07.

## 2026-10-05 — ground and cover

- **Got:** the three cover stages kept their shapes (IoU 0.96–0.997). The ground came out as bright cobblestones, not mud.
- **Decided:** in a game-size test the cover almost disappeared into the ground. The ground was edited (darker, softer, less contrast) instead of regenerated, to save time.
- **Trace:** ASSET-LOG E-01 to E-04; `design/asset-log/env/check_scene_v1.png` → `check_scene_v2.png`.

## 2026-10-05 — building and playing the slice

- **Human / Claude:** Claude wrote all the Godot code and the automated test. I set up the project, fixed the folder mix-up, reported errors, and played it.
- **Got:** one parse error in `enemy.gd` (fixed). The automated test passes 8/8.
- **My playtest:** no sound or music problems with sound on; readable with sound off. From my screenshots the health bar was hard to see, so it was changed to green / yellow / red.
- **Still unresolved (my notes):** the turret could turn faster, the hull turning could look smoother, and the enemy tanks should look different from YunqiZ.
- **Trace:** TEST-REPORT.md; `design/test/`.

## 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-07 — making the explainer film

- **Wanted:** the 4K explainer film with Brutalist's `godot-gamedev` skill in `walker` mode.
- **Asked:** Claude Code (in `brutalist.art`) to read the skill and build the film from my project, with a list of what the assignment requires. It checks the runtime, reads the code and documents, records real gameplay by driving the game itself, writes and voices the narration (local Kokoro), renders and exports.
- **Got / friction:**
  - My laptop battery was about to run out during the first gameplay recording. I had it stop the recording safely; the partial take could not be resumed (enemies move randomly), so it was recorded again from the start after I plugged in.
  - The render and the final export were stopped three times because the computer ran low on memory. I closed other programs; the last time, a leftover 8 GB `ffmpeg` from the killed export was still running, and Claude Code confirmed it was orphaned before re-running the export in the foreground.
  - The toolkit's quality check failed on 13 beats because the `@NikBearBrown` footer in one shared toolkit template (`GodotDesignFigure.tsx`) sat 3 px below the title-safe line at 4K.
- **Decided:** I allowed a local, uncommitted edit to that toolkit template (two numbers, matching its sibling template that already passed) and a re-render of the 13 beats, instead of rebuilding them on another layout (about 1.5 h more). My game was not changed and nothing was pushed to the toolkit.
- **Got:** a 4K film. Its own QC also pointed out that my committed ASSET-LOG was out of date (missing the environment rows), the HUD text has low contrast, and the mute and restart keys are not shown. I updated the documents afterwards; the film shows the commit it was built from.
- **Human / Claude / model:** Claude Code built the film end to end. I supplied the project and the requirements, made the battery, memory and toolkit decisions above, and watched and listened to the final film myself before accepting it. I watched and listened to the whole film and found no problems.

# walker-TANK

A tank-battle game in Godot: you drive **YunqiZ** through a ruined brick battlefield and destroy three enemy tanks.

- **Starting point:** my own Assignment 2 game and Assignment 3 3D asset room in this repository (A5 baseline commit `c4a1f84`). See [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).
- **Engine:** Godot 4.7.2 stable. **Renderer:** Forward+ (engine default; `project.godot` sets no renderer). 2D: 1280×720, stretch `canvas_items`, no `hdr_2d`.
- **Film (Assignment 5):** TBD.

## Assignment 5 — hit flash shader and brick surface materials

### What Assignment 5 added

- **Hit flash on YunqiZ (2D):** `shaders/hit_flash.gdshader` (`canvas_item`, hand-written by me) mixes the sprite colour toward red: `mix(COLOR.rgb, flash_color.rgb, hit_amount * flash_strength)`. `scripts/hit_flash_driver.gd`, attached by one line in `scripts/main.gd`, puts one shared ShaderMaterial on YunqiZ's hull and turret.
  - On `damaged` it sets `hit_amount` to 1.0, then fades it to 0.0 over 0.5 s of game time.
  - A new hit restarts the fade. Pause holds it. Death and respawn clear it.
  - Enemies have no material. The existing white `_flash()` is unchanged.
- **Brick materials (3D):** `shaders/brick_surface.gdshader` (`spatial`, hand-written by me). It projects the Poly Haven red_bricks_04 colour and roughness maps from object-space position, because `cover_wall.glb` has no UVs. Uniforms: `albedo_tint`, `brightness`, `roughness_scale`, `uv_scale`.
  - Two materials share it: `materials/cover_wall_intact.tres` on `CoverWall` (through the importer's Use External on `M_Brick`) and `materials/cover_wall_damaged.tres` on a new `CoverWall2` (surface override).
- **Hint experiment:** `scenes/hint_experiment.tscn` with `shaders/hint_experiment.gdshader`. It shows the same 3×1 grey PNG (64/128/192, `tools/make_hint_png.gd`) through a sampler with `source_color` (Quad A) and one without (Quad B).
- **Generated shader for comparison:** `shaders/standard_generated.gdshader` (Godot's *Convert to ShaderMaterial* in `scenes/scratch_standard.tscn`; not used by the game).
- **Tests:** `tests/test_hit_flash.gd`, `tests/test_materials.gd`, `tests/check_tools_parse.gd`. **Capture tools:** `tools/capture_hit_flash.gd`, `tools/capture_hint.gd`, `tools/capture_materials.gd`.
- **Documents:** [CHANGE-BRIEF](CHANGE-BRIEF.md) (with Revisions) · [TEST-REPORT](TEST-REPORT.md) · [MATERIALS](MATERIALS.md) · [LANGUAGE-NOTES](LANGUAGE-NOTES.md) · [FRICTIONAL](FRICTIONAL.md) · [SOURCES](SOURCES.md) · [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). Evidence: `logs/`, `docs/a5/`.

### Run (Windows, Git Bash, from the repo root)

```bash
GODOT="/d/CSYE7270/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe"   # as in scripts/run-test.sh line 5

# Import once after cloning
"$GODOT" --headless --path . --import

# The game (main scene, scenes/main.tscn); or open the project in the editor and press F5
"$GODOT" --path .

# The 3D asset room with the two brick walls; or open the scene in the editor and press F6
"$GODOT" --path . res://scenes/asset_room_3d.tscn

# The hint experiment
"$GODOT" --path . res://scenes/hint_experiment.tscn
```

**Tests**, always through the wrapper, one per call. The wrapper runs headless with `--fixed-fps`, a 120 s timeout, and a log in `logs/<name>_<fps>fps.log`. It exits 1 on any FAIL or on `SHADER ERROR` / `SCRIPT ERROR`.

```bash
bash scripts/run-test.sh test_hit_flash.gd 30
bash scripts/run-test.sh test_hit_flash.gd 60
bash scripts/run-test.sh test_hit_flash.gd 144
bash scripts/run-test.sh test_materials.gd 60
bash scripts/run-test.sh check_tools_parse.gd 60
bash scripts/run-test.sh check_a3_assets.gd 60
bash scripts/run-test.sh test_sound_triggers.gd 60
```

Results at `3d48047`: 50/50 at each rate, 76/76, 9/9, 18/18, 8/8, all exit 0 ([TEST-REPORT](TEST-REPORT.md)).

**Capture tools.** These need a real window, because headless draws nothing. Output goes to `docs/a5/captures/`.

```bash
"$GODOT" --path . --resolution 1280x720 --script res://tools/capture_hit_flash.gd
"$GODOT" --path . --resolution 1280x720 --script res://tools/capture_hint.gd
"$GODOT" --path . --resolution 1280x720 --script res://tools/capture_materials.gd
# optional: prefix every file, e.g. after a temporary shader edit
"$GODOT" --path . --resolution 1280x720 --script res://tools/capture_materials.gd -- --tag=shader_edit
```

The game and the two scenes can also be opened in the editor. The command-line scene runs above follow Godot's standard CLI and were not themselves recorded in my notes.

### Controls

Unchanged from Assignment 2 (table below): WASD / arrows move, mouse aims, left mouse / Space fires, Esc / P pauses, M / N mute music / SFX, R restarts after victory.

### Known limitations (A5, from my notes)

- The existing white `_flash()` still runs (the test sees modulate 2.2), but in play it is visually masked by the red at the moment of the hit.
- The pause rule (fade holds while paused) has only the headless check. I could not press Esc within 0.5 s.
- `reset_full()` on a living tank mid-fade would not clear the fade. The game only calls it after death.
- My named pixel P1 is covered by the turret. The brief's hull prediction does not apply there, and a recomputed turret value is in the brief's Revisions. P2 matched exactly.
- No game material uses a normal map. `red_bricks_04_nor_gl_1k.png` is only in the Step 4 scratch material, so the normal-map check is not applicable.
- The interface-sweep looks (wash-out, gloss, brick size) are recorded mostly as numbers. Several are still to confirm by eye.
- The helper bash/python scripts I ran were written by Claude chat and are not in the repo.

---

## Assignment 3

Assignment 3 adds a 3D asset room to this repository; the 2D game from Assignment 2 (below) is unchanged.

- **3D asset room:** `scenes/asset_room_3d.tscn` puts the three assets next to a grey 6.0 × 1.6 × 3.4 m box that stands in for the YunqiZ hull, under one light.
- **Three assets**, built from Blender cubes, 36 triangles each, exported to `assets/models/`:
  - `cover_wall` — broken brick cover wall, 4.0 × 1.0 × 1.8 m (includes one hand edit of my own)
  - `ammo_crate` — olive crate with an off-white stripe, 1.24 × 0.84 × 0.71 m
  - `tank_hedgehog` — three crossed steel beams, 1.794 × 1.794 × 1.400 m
- **Build and export scripts:** `tools/blender/build_cover_wall.py`, `build_ammo_crate.py`, `build_tank_hedgehog.py` rebuild each asset from nothing and check it; `tools/blender/export_glb.py` exports a `.blend` to `.glb`.
- **Headless check:** `tests/check_a3_assets.gd` measures each `.glb` in Godot (size, lowest Y, root scale, height axis): 18 / 18 PASS.
- **Final film:** [Watch on Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tCX0BUF_Jx4Uj2bW2vaNanxA3WYCKaQn/view?usp=drive_link) — `claude-liam-walker-tank-a3-assets.mp4` (3840×2160 landscape, 3:39), SHA-256 `b91f985d83d7ffed36f941aef078ee3efa676d958c6f58b1ad84931d95c98d8c`. It shows game-source revision `9baa12c`. Its beat sheet, script and evidence are in `youtube/claude-liam-walker-tank-a3-assets/`; the MP4 itself is not in Git.

**Versions:** Godot 4.7.2 · Blender 5.2.2 LTS · MCP for Blender add-on 1.8 (protocol 13) · Claude Code 2.1.299 (Opus 5.5) · Windows 11.

### Rebuild, export, import, check (Windows, Git Bash, from the repo root)

```bash
# Rebuild one asset from scratch in background Blender and check it (exit 0 = pass)
"/d/blender/blender.exe" -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python tools/blender/build_cover_wall.py
# (same for build_ammo_crate.py and build_tank_hedgehog.py)

# Export one .blend to .glb (one asset per call)
"/d/blender/blender.exe" -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 design/blender/cover_wall.blend --python tools/blender/export_glb.py -- assets/models/cover_wall.glb

# Godot: import, then the headless asset check (exit 0 = all pass, 1 = any FAIL, 124 = time limit hit)
GODOT="/d/CSYE7270/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64.exe/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe"
"$GODOT" --headless --path . --import
timeout 120 "$GODOT" --headless --path . --script res://tests/check_a3_assets.gd --fixed-fps 60
```

`timeout` is Git Bash's GNU `timeout`; Windows' own `timeout.exe` only waits and does not stop a program. To look at the assets, open the project in Godot 4.7 and open **`scenes/asset_room_3d.tscn`**.

### Known limitations (A3)

- The Blender build scripts check material slot names, not colour values, and say nothing about the asset after export.
- The Godot check measures each `.glb` on its own at the origin. It does not check the copies placed in `asset_room_3d.tscn`, colours, lighting, shadows or whether the shapes read correctly; I checked those by eye in the editor.
- With one light and no ambient fill, faces turned away from the light are very dark; how the colours look under the game's real lighting is not tested.
- Each asset is overlapping boxes, so hidden inside faces still count towards the 36 triangles.
- tank_hedgehog's "apply rotation" build step had no real rotation to apply (already baked during the join), so that step is untested.
- ammo_crate is 1.24 × 0.84 × 0.71 m, not the brief's 1.2 × 0.8 × 0.7, because the lid overhang and stripe were left out of the brief; it is inside the ±0.1 m tolerance.
- The cover_wall hand edit overshoots by 0.032 mm, inside the build check's 0.1 mm tolerance.
- The film shows my Blender session as my own screenshots (stills), not a screen recording, and the Godot scene with a static camera.
- The film shows Claude's plan and report but not the text of my prompt (my screenshots do not include it). In its last second the toolkit's locked outro mascot overlaps the @NikBearBrown handle.

Full details: [TEST-REPORT](TEST-REPORT.md) · [BLENDER-NOTES](BLENDER-NOTES.md) · [CHANGE-BRIEF](CHANGE-BRIEF.md) · [FRICTIONAL](FRICTIONAL.md) · [SOURCES](SOURCES.md). The Assignment 2 test report is in [docs/a2/TEST-REPORT.md](docs/a2/TEST-REPORT.md).

---

## Assignment 2

A tank-battle asset slice for CSYE7270 Assignment 2. You drive **YunqiZ**, a worn olive tank with a dozer blade and a white identification stripe, through a ruined brick battlefield: hide behind cover that breaks under fire, pick your moment, and destroy all three enemy tanks.

- **Started from:** an empty Godot 4 project (see [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md)).
- **Engine:** Godot 4.7.2 stable.
- **Film:** [Watch on Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1wZdhVj9YaA1GIYIu9yU09Xp2JRoVltxk/view?usp=drive_link) — `claude-liam-walker-tank-gamedev.mp4` (3840×2160 landscape), SHA-256 `b13a75400f8405be572142c3ab1c4565d49f980c2c82b4a6851c6b8d074fd150`

## Run

1. Open Godot 4.7, **Import** → select `project.godot` in this folder → open.
2. Press **F5**.

Automated sound-trigger check (after opening the project once so assets are imported):

```bash
godot --headless --path . -s res://tests/test_sound_triggers.gd
```

## Controls

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| WASD / arrow keys | Move (the hull faces the movement direction) |
| Mouse | Aim the turret |
| Left mouse button / Space | Fire (0.8 s reload) |
| Esc / P | Pause |
| **M** | Mute / unmute music |
| **N** | Mute / unmute sound effects |
| R | Play again after victory |

Music and sound are also toggled with the buttons at the top right.

## What the slice demonstrates

- **Character:** YunqiZ in 8 facings (5 generated with SDXL img2img, 3 mirrored), hull and turret as separate sprites, idle and moving states, recoil, hit flash, smoke at ≤60% health and fire at ≤30%, destruction.
- **Environment:** a generated ground tile and brick cover in three generated stages (intact, cracked after 2 hits, broken after 4 hits; broken cover no longer blocks).
- **Sound:** five generated sound effects on real events — fire, cover hit, YunqiZ hit, explosion, victory — each once per event.
- **Music:** a generated 8-bar loop at 70 BPM; pauses with the game, cuts on failure, restarts on respawn, stops at victory.
- **Loop:** three enemy tanks that move and fire back; respawn at the spawn point with destroyed enemies staying destroyed; victory screen.

## Known limitations

- Enemy tanks are the YunqiZ sprites tinted grey, not separate designs.
- Muzzle flash, explosions, smoke and fire are code particles, not generated art.
- The opening top-down zoom (storyboard panel 1) and the low-angle victory illustration (panel 8) were not built.
- The up and right turrets have no commander cupola; the other three do.
- Cannon and explosion sounds are mostly low frequency and may be quiet on laptop speakers.
- The hull snaps between 8 facings and the turret could turn more responsively.

## Documents

## The check failing on purpose

A check that has never failed may be broken. Claude ran a scratch copy of `check_a3_assets.gd` whose only difference (confirmed with `diff`) was ammo_crate's expected height changed from 0.71 to 0.81. It printed two FAIL lines and `RESULT: FAIL (2 failure(s))` with **exit code 1**; the other 16 checks still passed. The real script and the assets were not changed.

## What the checks do and do not show

- **The Blender build scripts** show that each asset can be rebuilt from nothing with the stated size, origin, applied transforms, triangle count and material slot *names*. They do not check colour values, and they say nothing about the asset after export.
- **The tank_hedgehog script's "apply rotation" step tested nothing.** The beams' rotation was already baked into the mesh during the join, so the bake step found identity transforms (it printed `identity: True`). The result is correct, but that step never had a real rotation to apply.
- **The Godot check** measures each `.glb` on its own, instantiated at the origin: size, lowest Y, root scale and the height axis, to 0.01 m. It does **not** check the copies placed in `asset_room_3d.tscn`, whether they rest on the floor there, colours, lighting, shadows, or whether the shapes read as what they are. Headless Godot uses a dummy renderer, so none of that is visible to it.
- **Hidden faces:** each asset is made of overlapping boxes, so faces inside the asset (the crate lid's underside, the wall's block bottoms, the hedgehog's crossing) still count towards the 36 triangles. They are never visible, so I left them.

## Problems found and what I changed

1. **tank_hedgehog's brief was wrong (evidence-based revision).** I asked Claude to work out the bounding box *before* building. With the brief's 2.4 m beams it came to 2.011 × 2.011 × **1.559** m, 0.009 m over the height tolerance, because the brief's numbers used the beam centrelines and left out the 0.15 m section. Claude recommended turning each beam 45° to fit. I chose instead to shorten the beams to **2.125 m**, because the overall size is what the game design depends on (lower than the 1.6 m hull, a barrier at hull scale), while the beam length was only a construction detail and was the number that was wrong. Result: 1.794 × 1.794 × 1.400 m. The change is recorded under *Revisions* in `CHANGE-BRIEF.md`; the original text is unchanged.
2. **ammo_crate's brief size left out the lid.** The brief lists the body size, but the lid overhangs by 0.02 m on each side and the stripe adds 0.01 m, so the real box is 1.24 × 0.84 × 0.71 m. Inside the ±0.1 m tolerance, so I kept it; the build script checks both the exact size and the brief tolerance.
3. **ammo_crate z-fighting avoided.** Claude noticed before building that a stripe exactly as deep as the lid (0.84 m) would share the lid's front and back faces and could flicker. I accepted its suggestion to make the stripe 0.83 m deep. The overall size did not change.
4. **My hand edit on cover_wall was 0.7 mm short.** I moved block B +0.6 m in Edit Mode. My sidebar then showed 4 m wide and I thought it was flush. Claude's read-only background inspection showed it had moved 0.5993 m, 0.7 mm short: **the sidebar rounds, so it could not show that error.** My correction (G X 0.0007, computed from a 4-decimal printout that was itself rounded) overshot by 0.032 mm. That is inside the build check's 0.1 mm tolerance and far below anything visible, so I stopped there. Lesson: to place something exactly, type the coordinate into the sidebar instead of nudging with G; and decide the tolerance first, then stop when inside it.

## HUMAN CHECK: look

*My own observations in the Godot editor (`scenes/asset_room_3d.tscn`), with the grey 6.0 × 1.6 × 3.4 m box standing in for the YunqiZ hull. Screenshot: `design/godot/asset_room_3d.png`.*

- **From the top** (the game's camera direction): the ammo crate's off-white stripe is the most readable feature in the scene, which is what the brief wanted. The hedgehog reads as three crossing beams. The wall's shadow shows its broken top, higher on the left.
- **Floor contact:** every asset casts a shadow that meets its base; none of them floats. (This is the check the headless script cannot do for the scene copies.)
- **Scale:** next to the hull box, the wall is wider than the hull is deep and lower than the turret would be, the crate is small enough to drive over, and the hedgehog is clearly lower than the hull. All three look in proportion.
- **From behind and below:** I switched the editor to the rear and bottom views for each asset. I saw no missing faces and no wrong colours; I found no problems to fix.
- **Not resolved:** with one light and no ambient fill, faces turned away from the light are very dark. The brief asked for one light; whether the game's real lighting suits these colours is not tested here.

## Brief failure cases, predicted vs. what happened

| # | Predicted | What happened |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lying on its side (Z-up vs Y-up) | Did not happen; height is on Godot Y for all three |
| 2 | Scale or rotation not applied | Did not happen; scale 1, 1, 1 in Blender and Godot. Building from mesh data meant scale was never non-1 |
| 3 | Origin in the middle, floats or sinks | Did not happen; lowest Y 0.0000 in Godot |
| 4 | Claude builds more than asked | Did not happen; 36 triangles each, 3 boxes each |
| 5 | Colours lost on export | Did not happen; colours visible in the Godot screenshot (checked by eye, not measured) |
| 6 | MCP will not connect on Windows | Connected, after one failed command (see FRICTIONAL.md) |

Not predicted: the hedgehog's brief size being wrong, the crate's lid overhang, and a Blender error (`AttributeError ... 'select_set'`) during cover_wall's join.

# TEST-REPORT — Assignment 3: three 3D assets

The Assignment 2 report has moved, unchanged, to `docs/a2/TEST-REPORT.md`.

**Versions:** Blender 5.2.2 LTS · MCP for Blender add-on 1.8 (protocol 13) · Godot 4.7.2 · Claude Code 2.1.299 (Opus 5.5) · Windows 11, RTX 3060 laptop.

**How to re-run the checks (Windows, Git Bash, from the repo root):**

```bash
# Blender: rebuild each asset from scratch and check it (exit 0 = pass)
"/d/blender/blender.exe" -b --factory-startup --python-exit-code 1 --python tools/blender/build_cover_wall.py
# (same for build_ammo_crate.py and build_tank_hedgehog.py)

"$GODOT" --headless --path . --import
timeout 120 "$GODOT" --headless --path . --script res://tests/check_a3_assets.gd --fixed-fps 60
```

The course commands are written for macOS. On Windows I use Git Bash's GNU `timeout` (coreutils 8.32), because Windows' own `timeout.exe` only waits and does not stop a program; and `--path .` because my Godot project is the repo root, not a `godot/` folder.

## Results

All sizes in metres. Blender is Z-up, Godot is Y-up, so a Blender (x, y, z) size appears in Godot as (x, z, y).
